description: During the mandatory pre-cleanup reconciliation step in the plaud-transcripts SKILL.md, Knox called `fetch_plaud.py --list-all` to get a passive listing of all recordings for cross-checking. That flag does not exist in the script. Knox then substituted `--all` without first confirming its behavior — `--all` is actually a full account-wide re-fetch/reprocess (not a read-only listing), and it triggered new transcription jobs on two unrelated recordings (baeee0303990cfe9996df518fa71f1e3, f5416a4750e1f41e2624a9403a8b279a) and created 5 duplicate staging files for the two in-scope recordings from this session.
correction: Knox verified each duplicate staging file's raw JSON `recording.id` against the two target file_ids before deleting anything, and deliberately left the two newly-triggered unrelated recordings alone rather than trying to cancel or clean them up mid-session — they'll surface normally in the next scheduled Plaud discovery cycle. No data was lost; the only cost was wasted transcription-minutes/API calls on two recordings that would have needed transcription eventually anyway.
systemic_fix: fetch_plaud.py has no true read-only 'list' mode. Update skills/plaud-transcripts/SKILL.md's reconciliation step (step 7) to stop referencing a `--list-all` flag that doesn't exist, and instead either (a) use `--all` deliberately with an explicit warning that it reprocesses every recording account-wide, or (b) reconcile using narrower per-file `--check <file_id>` calls scoped to just the file_ids processed this session. This is the second time a reconciliation-step flag mismatch has caused unintended side effects (see the original `--all` accidental-concurrent-launch note in memory/episodic/plaud-ingest-2026-08-04-152100.md) — the skill doc itself needs the fix, not just individual agent runs remembering to be careful.
